claim: A task-energy-tank and passivity-based shaping mechanism can coordinate variable impedance, force control, and periodic DMP motion so that a human can physically adapt a tactile manipulation skill while the robot bounds exchanged energy and subsequently executes the adapted skill autonomously.
epistemic_status: Author-reported method and experimental evidence, with conditional inference about scope and safety.
problem_and_setting: Learning and adapting contact-rich robotic skills under unified force-impedance control, where variable stiffness and human physical interaction may compromise passivity. Skills are decomposed into contact initiation, manipulation, and termination; manipulation combines periodic DMP motion with a force policy.
method_or_mechanism: The controller uses a task-energy tank and passivity-based shaping function to coordinate impedance and force behavior. It limits available task energy while allowing physical human interaction to modify periodic motion shape and frequency. When the energy bound is approached, impedance shaping is reduced and stiffness may fall to zero. A contact-loss handler smoothly modifies force shaping during loss and recovery.
content_summary: Franka Emika experiments center on polishing, with video demonstrations also showing unscrewing and levering. In autonomous circular motion with Smax=14 J, a human changes speed while energy shaping limits impedance and can reduce stiffness to zero. In contact polishing with a 5 N desired force and Smax=2 J, a human adapts motion shape and frequency, after which the robot autonomously repeats the updated skill. During contact loss, the handler smoothly reduces commanded z-force from 5 N to 0 and restores it to 5 N. Maximum energy allowance is predefined and broader validation is limited.
synthesis_role: Provides a concrete energy-tank design pattern for passivity-aware physical adaptation of periodic contact skills under variable impedance and force control, while exposing energy-budget selection and validation breadth as unresolved issues.
development_link: Supports human-guided online adaptation with explicit task-energy regulation; motivates learned or context-dependent Smax and force learning through stiffness adaptation.

evidence.locator: Method: tactile-skill decomposition and manipulation controller
evidence.finding: Skills use three primitives; manipulation combines periodic DMP motion with a force policy governed by task-energy-tank/passivity shaping.
With Smax=14 J, a human changes motion speed; when energy exceeds the limit, impedance shaping decreases and stiffness can reach zero.
At 5 N desired force and Smax=2 J, a human adapts shape and frequency, and the robot then executes the updated skill autonomously.
The force command changes smoothly from 5 N to 0 after contact loss and returns to 5 N after re-contact.
Smax is predefined; force learning through stiffness adaptation and online Smax decision remain future work.

boundary_conditions: Passivity is conditional on the energy-tank formulation.
The stability interpretation assumes a passive environment.
Experiments use a Franka Emika and primarily polishing.
Other tasks are mainly video demonstrations.
Evidence does not establish universal safety or stability.
assumptions: Energy-tank bookkeeping is implemented as formulated.
The DMP and force policy represent the skill.

reported: Smax is predefined rather than learned.
Force learning through stiffness adaptation is not implemented.
Decision-making for Smax is future work.
inferred: Unreported participant count and statistics limit repeatability conclusions.
One principal polishing use case limits generality.
Passivity is not universal collision safety or safety under non-passive environments.
